title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: Viet-Khoa Tran-Nguyen (Université Paris Cité) and Pedro J. Ballester (Imperial College London) propose community guidelines for evaluating deep-learning scoring functions used in protein–ligand pose generation and binding-affinity prediction. They argue cross-study comparison is currently unreliable and call for transparent data and code, guards against data leakage and sampling bias, common data splits, run-to-run variability checks and baselines. Only the abstract is available; the body is paywalled.

themes.theme: Evaluation crisis in AI scoring functions

insights.claim: Deep-learning scoring functions have recently gained prominence in protein–ligand pose generation and binding-affinity prediction for computational drug design, but several shortcomings make it increasingly difficult to evaluate them for a specific task across studies.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Reported benchmark gains from AI drug-discovery tools may not be comparable, so performance claims by AI-biotech vendors deserve scrutiny.
insights.quote: several shortcomings make it increasingly difficult to evaluate scoring functions for a specific task across studies.

insights.claim: Tran-Nguyen and Ballester argue that data leakage, sampling bias and flawed study design must be guarded against when evaluating structure-based protein–ligand binding prediction methods.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Leakage-inflated results suggest real-world hit rates of AI docking and affinity models may fall short of published numbers.
insights.quote: Guarding against data leakage, sampling bias and flawed design is equally important.

insights.claim: The guidelines say transparent disclosure of training data, code and procedures is essential for reproducibility, reuse and independent scrutiny of AI scoring functions for protein–ligand binding.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Closed, undisclosed models in AI drug discovery may face growing credibility pressure from the research community.
insights.quote: Transparent disclosure of training data, code and procedures is essential to permit reproducibility, reuse and independent scrutiny.

insights.claim: According to the guidelines, meaningful comparison of protein–ligand scoring functions requires common data splits, checks for run-to-run variability and performance baselines.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Standardized benchmarks would make it easier to tell which AI drug-design methods genuinely outperform classical docking.
insights.quote: Meaningful comparisons of scoring functions also require common data splits, checks for run-to-run variability and performance baselines.

insights.claim: The guidelines paper by Viet-Khoa Tran-Nguyen and Pedro J. Ballester was funded by EPSRC, the Wolfson Foundation, the Royal Society and France's ANR, was received 15 January 2026 and published 23 October 2026, and the authors declare no competing interests.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Academic, non-commercial authorship positions the guidelines as a neutral benchmark standard rather than vendor marketing.
